Lemma
[Evolution of the area of a minimizing disk] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0264, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iv:page-0265 ↗ lem:chow-iv-minimizing-disk-first-variation 1. ch33:33.28\group Minimal disks

For every $A\in (0,\widetilde A)$ and $\varepsilon >0$, at all sufficiently large times a minimizing disk $D(t)$ satisfies \[ \frac{d^+A_{\mathfrak T_A}}{dt}(t)\le -2\pi +(1+\varepsilon )^{1/2}L_{g(t)}(\partial D(t)) -(1+\varepsilon )^{-1/2}A_{\mathfrak T_A}(t). \]

Proof

\sketch The average and minimum scalar curvatures tend to $-6$, so the interior term in the first-variation bound is at most $-(1-\varepsilon )A_{\mathfrak T_A}$. In an exact cusp the relevant boundary geodesic curvature is one; smooth convergence of the piece to a cusp makes its integral at most $(1+\varepsilon )L$. The normal velocity tends uniformly to zero. Renaming $\varepsilon $ gives the displayed estimate.

□
